pool.text: Spanish conquistador Pedro Arias Dávila founded the city of Panama on August 15.
Genoese merchants controlled the port and regional commerce thanks to a Spanish concession.
The city served as the starting point for expeditions conquering Peru's Inca Empire.
Gonzalo Fernández de Oviedo y Valdés published the first story about Panama.
Henry Morgan and his men attacked, looted, and destroyed the original city by fire.
The Panama Railroad Company's railroad began full operation across the isthmus.
Panama declared independence from Colombia and Philippe Bunau-Varilla was named minister.
The National Theater was founded as one of the main monuments.
The Panama Canal was completed and symbolized United States influence.
Events known as Martyrs' Day erupted on January 9.
The United States transferred full control of the Panama Canal to Panama.
The historic district of Panama City was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Trump Organization built the Trump Ocean Club as its first Latin American investment.
The city achieved the second highest hotel occupancy rate for any city outside the United States.
UNESCO decided that Casco Viejo would not be placed on the World Heritage in Danger list.
Hilton Worldwide opened The Panamera, the second Waldorf Astoria Hotel in Latin America.
President Ricardo Martinelli built the Cinta Costera 3 maritime highway viaduct extension.
The Trump Ocean Club building was renamed The Bahia Grand Panama following falling occupancy rates.
